A computer-solved model has been used to predict the homeostatic concentrations which arise from varying degrees of… 24872571 homeostasis model assessment insulin resistance cell function from The steady-state basal plasma glucose and insulin concentrations are Homeostasis model assessment: insulin resistance and β-cell function from fasting plasma glucose and insulin concentrations in man The steady-state basal plasma glucose and insulin concentrations are determined by their interaction in a feedback loop. A computer-solved model has been used to predict the homeostatic concentrations which arise from varying degrees of β-cell deficiency and insulin resistance. Comparison of a patient's fasting values with the model's predictions allows a quantitative assessment of the contributions of insulin resistance and deficient β-cell function to the fasting hyperglycaemia (homeostasis model assessment, HOMA). The accuracy and precision of the estimate have been determined by comparison with independent measures of insulin resistance and β-cell function
